CHECK 1 — scope screening of the four proposals against the scope contract (BEHAVIOUR, HYPERBOLIC, REAL COUPLING, TESTABLE EFFECT, MINIMAL SPEC).
Read: all four proposal texts and their frozen bundles (each bundle shares the same OBSERVED block: [E5] successor-entropy stratification, [E6] width-20 beam survival, [E7] teacher-forced per-position NLL, [E8] level-1 capacity ceiling, [E9] cohort-profile signal, [E10] train-only edge stats, [E11] SID prefix diagnostic).
Observed: all four name a train-only directed-transition signal and an explicit curved operation inside the RQ quantizer, and all four contain a connected pathway (behaviour enters the same assignment/recursion as the curved geometry), so none is out of scope on grounds 1-3. All four supply equations, inputs/outputs, safeguards and a cost estimate; curvature is fixed c=1 in warp-rq, moeb-rq and aniso-rq, while STATECELL derives c from the 99th-percentile encoder norm and derives tau_l from the median nearest-code distance. Switches: aniso-rq and STATECELL state the three switch states explicitly; warp-rq states only the identity-frame comparison and moeb-rq states "neither switch preserves the other" (weaker but present).
Open: which evidence differentiates them on plausibility of reaching Recall@10 > 0.065.

CHECK 2 — evidence that discriminates the candidates (E6, E7, E8, E9, E11, E10).
Read: [E6] beam survival on 57,439 test rows; [E7] per-position NLL; [E8] K-sweep of positive-pair co-location; [E11] same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067; [E10] 115,582 distinct train edges / 118,315 edges, mean out-degree 5.45.
Observed: (a) no arm in the bundle reaches the 0.065 target; the best is resample 0.06363, then l1_only 0.06233 and l1_br_euclid 0.06207. (b) The c=1 hyperbolic quantizer arm l1_br is the WORST (recall@10 0.04671) and is degenerate: gold prefix alive at depth 1/2/3 = 1.000/1.000/1.000 with T1/T2/T3 NLL 0.00/0.00/0.00 and T4 NLL 9.03 — i.e. the first three Poincare-coded levels are constant, so prefix survival is trivial and all information is pushed into one deep position. Euclidean l1_br_euclid recovers structure (depth 2/3 = 0.829/0.161, NLL 3.22/4.36). (c) The binding bottleneck for Stage 3 is therefore gold-prefix survival at depth 2/3 (0.829/0.161 best case) and T2/T3 NLL — not level-1 width. (d) [E8]: behavioural co-location at K=256 is 0.0822 positive vs 0.0129 negative (6.4x lift) but small in absolute terms, so cell boundaries must be shifted substantially to capture it. (e) [E9] 0.9291 vs 0.8871 and [E11] 0.0907 vs 0.067 show a real but modest train-only behaviour signal, so a coupling that is capped/derived rather than free is the right design.
Reasoning consequence: a fixed c=1 Poincare quantizer with a 1e-3 r_max is the exact configuration the bundle shows collapsing; only STATECELL-MARGIN-RQ escapes it (data-derived curvature scale, data-derived per-level margin), and it attacks the measured depth-2/3 prefix bottleneck directly by making successor items share codes. warp-rq and moeb-rq both sit in the c=1 regime; aniso-rq both sits in c=1 and bounds its stretch at sqrt(2), below what [E8] implies is needed.
Open: nothing further; ready to rank.

FINAL ANSWER — ranking of the four proposals (single JSON object, requested format).
Ranking rationale per proposal:
1 STATECELL-MARGIN-RQ: only proposal with a derived curvature scale (c from 99th-pct encoder norm) — escapes the c=1 collapse of arm l1_br (E6 recall 0.04671, E7 T1/T2/T3 NLL 0.00/0.00/0.00, T4 9.03); derives tau_l from the median nearest-code distance at init instead of tuning it; behaviour term is a successor-code distribution over the codebook alphabet, which is exactly the depth-2/3 prefix predictability that E6 (gold prefix alive 0.829/0.161) and E7 (T2/T3 NLL 3.22/4.36) show caps recall; margin cap of one typical quantization unit is consistent with E8 (K=256 co-location 0.0822 vs 0.0129, real but small absolute) and E11 (0.0907 vs null 0.067). Switches explicit.
2 succframe-warp-rq: real determinant-one behaviour metric entering every level's distance, warp strength derived from the eigenvalue share of the successor second moment, which E5 supports (top-1 mass 0.4375 vs 0.0543 across quintiles); but fixed c=1 with r_max = 1-1e-3 and artanh clipping is the regime E6/E7 show to degenerate; per-epoch frame refresh is non-stationary and the identity-frame check is post-hoc only.
3 SUCCFRAME-MOEB-RQ: coupling is genuine and cheap (1.02-1.10x), but every encoding step is a Mobius isometry, so items with similar anchors are assigned a translated codebook (a relabeling that only per-item anchor spread breaks); fixed c=1 again, tau=atanh(0.5) and rho=0.5 are documented defaults rather than measured quantities, the geodesic loss replaces the baseline loss (attribution confound that one run cannot separate), and E5/E10 (mean out-degree 5.45, tail 2.7 successors) make the near-origin anchor common.
4 beh-aniso-poincare-rq: scope-valid but weakest — c=1 fixed, beta in [0,1] collapses the stretch to at most sqrt(2) along one direction, which E8 (6.4x lift available at K=256 but only 0.0822 absolute) implies is too mild to move prefix membership; tangent Frechet codebook updates risk usage collapse; smallest stated gain (<5% wall clock) corresponds to the smallest geometric change.

STEP 1 — Scope check of the four proposals against the five in-scope conditions.
Read: the frozen evidence bundles b446d876c2868ce3 (succframe-warp-rq), e73b8eb1c7c940d1 (beh-aniso-poincare-rq), 3f0b0e98e5eaa49d (STATECELL-MARGIN-RQ), 7c4d9919976eaa7c (SUCCFRAME-MOEB-RQ), plus the shared observed items E4–E11 in each bundle.
Observed per proposal:
- succframe-warp-rq: behaviour = directed adjacent transitions A (E2-style), geometry = per-item determinant-one warp W_i of the Poincare chord inside every RQ level's nearest-code rule and reconstruction/commitment term; coupling is real (W_i enters d^W and the loss), switches exist; cost +10–20%. Weaknesses I note: codebook parameters/updates stay Euclidean-unaware while the metric is per-item, so no single codebook point minimises the per-item warped objective (internally inconsistent objective); W_i is recomputed from the drifting current encoder each epoch (moving metric, non-stationary); constants 0.8 mass coverage, exp(0.5*alpha) and sqrt(d) clip are semi-arbitrary; the hypothesis needs a second, post-hoc identity-frame assignment code path.
- beh-aniso-poincare-rq: behaviour = successor resultant direction u_i and concentration beta_i, geometry = anisotropic Poincare gauge inside assignment; coupling real. Defects: the spec never gives the formula for beta_i (it says only "obtain beta_i in [0,1]"), so the minimal-specification condition is not met; stretch is bounded by sqrt(2); the codebook update is changed to tangent Frechet means (collapse risk); the "geometry off" switch is written as c->0, which is at best the flat limit of the same distance, sloppily specified.
- STATECELL-MARGIN-RQ: behaviour = popularity-adjusted (w_ij = c_ij/sqrt(1+c_j)) directed successor distribution restricted to top-10, evaluated over the hierarchy's OWN code alphabet (n_ik over Succ(i)); geometry = Poincare geodesic distance squared with curvature derived from the 99th percentile encoder norm (E12); coupling real, since the margin tau_l*(clip(log q/log(1/K),0,1)-1) is added to d2_ik inside the same argmin, and removing either term changes the selected code. Constants derived: tau_l = median_i min_k d2_ik (median nearest-code distance, frozen); no tuned constant; cost 5–15%. Testable observables: level-1 prefix-match rate, H(code_1(next)|code_1(cur)), Stage-3 recall@10.
- SUCCFRAME-MOEB-RQ: behaviour = train-only transition SVD anchor, frozen; geometry = Mobius subtraction/addition as the residual recursion with exact inverse decode and geodesic reconstruction loss; coupling real and exact (encode/decode isometry). Defects: it REPLACES the baseline squared-Euclidean reconstruction loss with a geodesic one, an acknowledged confound that one non-ablated run cannot separate; tau = atanh(0.5) and rho = 0.5 are documented defaults but arbitrary; deep (level 2/3) codes are re-expressed as offsets from the successor region, which changes exactly the deep prefix bits that identify the item.
Nothing found that puts a proposal out of scope outright; succframe-warp-rq and beh-aniso carry specification/objective-integrity defects; the other two satisfy all five conditions.
Open at this point: quantify which mechanism the observed evidence (E6/E11/E8) favours.

STEP 2 — Evidence-grounded ranking calculation.
Read: shared observed items. Key numbers I use:
E6 (width-20 beam survival, 57,439 test rows): behaviour/geometry-aggressive variants all sit BELOW the flat/Euclidean controls — successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500, l1_br 0.04671; the flat controls sit at l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363. Gold-prefix survival at depth 1/2/3/4 for the good variants is 1.000/0.829/0.156–0.161/0.085, i.e. the binding constraint is the exact SID (depth-4) being inside the beams, and l1_br shows what goes wrong when depth 1–3 is forced perfectly alive (1.000/1.000/1.000) while exact SID dies (0.068) — prefix co-location alone does not convert to recall, it eats identity resolution.
E11: same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 against permuted null 0.067 — the existing SIDs already carry only a thin successor/prefix co-location signal, so a behaviour margin has real but small headroom and must be bounded or it will destroy identity bits (the l1_br failure mode).
E8: at K=256 only 0.0822 of canonical pairs share a first-level cluster (negatives 0.0129); the level-1 capacity is tight, so anything that spends level-1 on co-location must be capped.
E9: positive shares a successor cohort 0.9291 vs 0.8871 for fixed negatives — behaviour signal is real but the margin (about +0.04) is modest, favouring a discounted/bounded use.
E5/E10: successor structure is genuinely stratified (top-1 mass 0.4375 low-entropy vs 0.0543 high-entropy; mean outgoing degree 5.45, 115,582 distinct edges), so per-item successor statistics are estimable — this supports all four but especially the ones that use them as a bounded shift rather than a metric.
Reasoning: STATECELL is the only proposal whose behaviour term is popularity-discounted (w_ij = c_ij/sqrt(1+c_j)) AND hard-capped at one quantization unit by a DERIVED tau_l (median nearest-code distance), i.e. it is explicitly engineered against the two failure modes the evidence exhibits (hot-cell/prefix-degeneration like l1_br and identity destruction at depth 4), while acting on the one quantity the beam data says matters (successor prefix co-location), and it has no tuned constant. SUCCFRAME-MOEB is the cleanest mathematically (exact isometry, frozen anchors, <1% cost) but it rewrites the residual path so that level-2/3 bits become offsets from a behaviour anchor — directly attacking the depth-4 identity resolution that E6 shows is already at 0.085 — and it replaces the reconstruction loss (acknowledged confound). beh-aniso is the least harmful but the least specified (no beta_i formula) and its stretch bound sqrt(2) plus the healthy likelihood it is a no-op put it mid-low. succframe-warp-rq is closest in family to the variants that already failed in E6 (per-item geometric warping, tangent_successor_residual 0.0550 / successor_geodesic_coarse 0.0550), leaves the codebooks solving an inconsistent objective, refreshes the metric from a drifting encoder every epoch, and carries the highest cost (+10–20%); it ranks last.
Ranking: 1 STATECELL-MARGIN-RQ, 2 SUCCFRAME-MOEB-RQ, 3 beh-aniso-poincare-rq, 4 succframe-warp-rq.
Open: objection wording for the top pick.

STEP 3 — FINAL ANSWER (complete, self-contained).
